title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the 1986 notes on 'ateliers', Grothendieck is building an axiomatic, combinatorial framework for tame ('modérée') stratified geometry. An atelier A is a stock of elementary pieces (cells, 'atoms'). An A-figure is something like a finite stratified set or cell complex built from them. Here F denotes the set of A-figures. Each figure F has an underlying set of cells F~ (identified with F, written F~ || F), carrying an incidence order. There is a refinement relation G << F ('G is finer than F'), and an open/interior containment Y <<° X.

This page defines when a refinement is a subdivision.

Setup. Given G << F, there is an increasing (order-preserving) map phi: G~ -> F~. It sends each cell Y of G to the unique cell X = phi(Y) of F whose interior contains it (Y <<° X). In modern terms this is the 'carrier map' of a refinement of a cell or stratified decomposition.

Definition attempts. G is a subdivision of F if one of the following holds.
(i) For every cell X of F, the fibre phi^{-1}(X) satisfies phi^{-1}(X) <<° X. One automatically has supp° phi^{-1}(X) ⊂ X°. The requirement is equality: the cells of G lying over X exactly tile the open cell X°.
(ii) supp G = supp F. Here supp = supp°, the open support; the figures cover the same underlying set.
(iii) There is no atom Z in A with Z << F and Z disjoint (in the open sense, ||°) from G. This is a 'no hole' criterion tested on elementary pieces.

The equivalence (i) <=> (ii) <=> (iii) is claimed under an extra axiom on supports, written 'Atmag supp?'. That axiom is flagged with a question mark as not yet settled.

The next page adds two more conditions:
- (iv) a point-wise version for 'divisible' ateliers, testing with points x in L;
- (v) G is maximal among refinements of F under inclusion.
It also contains a crossed-out alternative: the Alexandrov topology of F~ is the quotient of that of G~.

Purpose: to get a notion of subdivision of stratified figures inside the atelier axiomatics. This is the combinatorial backbone of a tame topology in the sense of the Esquisse §5-6. It serves the preceding page's question of constructing the complement A \ N (the 'maquette' case), and probably invariance results under subdivision.
errors: The equivalences (i)<=>(ii)<=>(iii) are only claimed conditionally. They rest on an unformulated axiom ('Atmag supp?'). The next page admits that the implication back to (i) was 'supposed', not proved.
In (i) the inclusion supp° phi^{-1}(X) ⊂ X° is automatic, so the real content is the reverse inclusion. The first, struck-out wording ran the two together; this is a presentation issue, not an error.

ideas.what: Carrier map phi: G~ -> F~ from the cells of a refinement to the cells of the coarser figure, sending a cell to the unique cell whose interior contains it; it is order-preserving
ideas.modern_name: carrier map of a subdivision / refinement of stratifications (face-poset map)
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical combinatorial topology (Alexander, Whitehead); stratification theory (Whitney, Thom, Mather)
ideas.where_published: Tame topology programme announced in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5-6; the atelier formalism itself is unpublished

ideas.what: Definition of subdivision as a refinement with the same support, equivalently fibrewise tiling of open cells, equivalently no uncovered atom
ideas.modern_name: subdivision of a cell decomposition / refinement of o-minimal cell decompositions
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical PL topology; in the tame setting, o-minimality (van den Dries, Knight-Pillay-Steinhorn)

ideas.what: Axiomatic 'atelier' framework: tame geometry built from atoms and figures with refinement relations and open supports
ideas.modern_name: axiomatic tame topology (comparable to o-minimal structures or abstract cell/stratified categories)
ideas.usually_credited_to: o-minimality: van den Dries, Pillay-Steinhorn, Knight (1984-1998)
ideas.where_published: Only the programme is in the Esquisse; the atelier notes are unpublished

missed.claim: Grothendieck's axiomatic 'atelier' notion of subdivision for tame figures is never completed. The key support axiom ('Atmag supp?') is left open, as is the equivalence of the local (i) and global (ii, iii, v) characterisations.
missed.quote: Si on admet Atmag supp?, on voit que ceci équivaut à chacune des deux conditions
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a small piece of an unpublished, purely combinatorial axiomatisation of tame topology, independent of o-minimality. Comparing it with o-minimal cell decompositions or exit-path/stratified homotopy theory could be of historical and perhaps conceptual interest. The page itself contains only standard definitions.

deep.surprise_reason: The page gives a careful but essentially standard definition of subdivision of cell or stratified figures, with routine equivalent formulations. Its interest lies only in documenting Grothendieck's unpublished atelier axiomatics for tame topology, not in any new result.
transcription_corrections: The vertical marks under G~ and F~ are rotated '=' signs: G~ = G, F~ = F, i.e. the sets of cells are identified with the figures. The same applies under supp G and supp F, meaning supp G = supp° G and supp F = supp° F.
In the opening line, 'atelier' is written above a struck-out word, consistent with the transcription.
In (iii), 'Z ||° G' is a disjointness relation (open-disjoint), rendered as Z |°| G on the next page.
In (iii), the first 'Z' was written over a struck-out letter, and 'G' in 'Z ||° G' over a crossed-out symbol.
The margin note is largely illegible. It starts 'Il valait mieux ici...' and seems to be a remark about the atelier axiom; the transcription's guesses should be treated as tentative.
